messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: done refactoring math/matrix and agrad/matrix
parts:
Whew. That took about 12 hours longer than the
hour or two I'd anticipated. A lot of cruft
had built up of both the needless templating and
cut-and-paste variety.

I did a complete review of the matrix and
agrad/matrix implementations and cut out a lot
of the underbrush and pushed the domain checks
into reusable functions.

It was a fun read because some of the implementations
in there are really clever.

Because we know all the possible template instantiations
ahead of time, we could move the rest of the function definitions
from header (.hpp) to definition (_def.hpp) files, then
adding instantiation (_inst.cpp) along the same lines
we used for grammars. This would further speed up compilation
as the matrix stuff is pretty heavy. We could do the same
with distributions and eventually even have reasonably fast
compilation. (By the way, I'd like to eventually change matrix
back to this this header, definition, instantiation pattern,
too, because it allows the lib to be used header only by
including the _def.hpp files rather than the .hpp files -- there's
a long discussion of this in Vandeverde and Josuttis's C++
Templates book.)

The only change should from a user or Stan perspective
is that the lib throws std::domain_error instead
of segfaulting :-)

- Bob
